title: Extreme Complier Expected-Shortfall Ratios When Noncomplier Tails Mask a Shrinking First Stage
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision PASS with no findings; delivered tier=subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 7.0 < 7.4; salvageable=false within calibrated known-compliance Hall benchmark scope. Independent terminal-validity consult confirms the structural ceiling.
gap_reasons: Its scope is the calibrated no-covariate experiment with known compliance shares and fixed public tail envelopes, rather than a general weak-IV tail-inference framework.
The full procedure's conservative radius returns the entire public target range for every sample through n=2^20, so rate-optimal honesty does not establish practically informative inference.
The projected score is constrained by the narrow calibration and absent evidence of useful finite-sample performance, rather than a missing converse or an assumed achievability step.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed matching full-mixture minimax absolute-risk and honest-interval-length orders, including the logarithmic extrapolation factor, plus the background-disclosure versus complier-label separation. D0.5 mathematics and decision referees passed with no findings; the cold general referee capped the calibrated known-compliance Hall benchmark at subfield, and an independent terminal-validity consultation found no faithful within-scope route to field. No mathematical claim was reported refuted, and no Lean formalization was attempted; reuse the informal derivations and receipts without representing them as kernel-checked proofs.
tldr: Upper-tail complier effects remain identified when a randomized encouragement has declining compliance, but observed extreme outcomes may come chiefly from noncompliers. The focal result is the sharp absolute-error and honest expected-length frontier for the log ratio of extreme complier expected shortfalls in a fixed Hall benchmark. Its attainable estimator and connected interval must be total on every sample and honest at every finite sample size. The converse retains all four IV cells and normalized causal alternatives. A comparison of background disclosure, compliance labels, and removal of background upper tails isolates the information cost of hidden labels under masking.
gap: Fixed-level CRESTE inference and extreme-IV tail extrapolation do not determine the primitive information frontier when the first stage shrinks and the observed nuisance tail is heavier than the complier tail. Existing direct-sample Hall results evaluate a different likelihood.
fill: The core binds matching all-procedure lower bounds, a total observable estimator, finite-sample uniform coverage, and expected interval-length attainment in the same full experiment. The exact numerical rate and threshold are outputs of the open question.
